inputs.original_text: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent jumped into action after a baby stuck in a crowded TSA line with his family stopped breathing at JFK International Airport in New York on Thursday. Video footage released by the Department of Homeland Security showed a man holding a baby notice something wrong with the child and begin ...
inputs.modified_text: A baby stopped breathing in a crowded TSA line at JFK on Thursday, and an ICE agent stepped in while the family was in distress. That deserves recognition as a humane act—but the Department of Homeland Security releasing footage doesn’t turn one moment into proof that an entire enforcement system serves everyone fairly. We can appreciate an individual helping a family and still ask why public safety is so often framed as a defense of institutions rather than a commitment to protecting vulnerable people consistently.
